title.narrative: Modern Cooking for Healthy Forests in Malawi - Tiphike Mwa Makono

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Modern Cooking for Healthy Forests (MCHF) activity promotes sustainable forest management in select landscapes and alternative clean energy options for cooking in targeted urban areas to reduce illegal charcoal use, which is the main driver of deforestation.MCHF will utilize FY2022 Climate Change-Adaptation funds to strengthen diversified livelihoods; increase incomes and assets of vulnerable communities and micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs); reduce communities' vulnerability to climate change impacts; leverage economic opportunities; and improve natural resource management. Specifically, MCHF will build the capacity of over 30 early-stage entrepreneurs and other established companies promoting clean cooking solutions and forest-/restoration-friendly enterprises to reduce an over-dependence on charcoal use and help restore degraded lands. By growing MSMEs and supporting entrepreneurs, MCHF helps Malawians move away from more climate-sensitive livelihoods. MCHF will also continue to support forest governance at local levels, working with stakeholders to develop forest management plans; collect and use data; build the capacity of village natural resources management, including their understanding and awareness of issues of tenure, access rights, and benefit sharing; conflict resolution; and forest fire prevention and management. USAID will support community groups to scale-up land restoration in degraded hot spots to create healthy ecosystems, diversify livelihoods, and reduce climate risk thereby increasing community and ecosystem resilience to climate variability.This activity supports the Mission's Integrated Country Strategy Objective 2.3 - Nurture entrepreneurship, unleashing the ingenuity of the Malawian people to self-realize a better economic future. .
